summary: Shell command injection in manual SEP lifecycle workflow
description:
## Summary
The manual SEP lifecycle workflow embeds the `issue_number` workflow_dispatch input directly into a shell `run` block. GitHub renders `${{ }}` expressions before the shell starts, so shell metacharacters and command substitutions in this input execute on the runner.

Affected revision: `4df2d6b6e3588efb46e7542d98498e5c630a0a86` (latest `main` as of 2026-08-14).
File: `.github/workflows/sep-lifecycle-manual.yml`
Relevant lines: [56-58](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/4df2d6b6e3588efb46e7542d98498e5c630a0a86/.github/workflows/sep-lifecycle-manual.yml#L56-L58)

## Reproduction
1. Trigger the workflow manually using an account permitted to dispatch it.
2. Set `issue_number` to the inert value `$(printf INJECTED)`.
3. The resulting shell script includes:

```sh
if [[ -n "$(printf INJECTED)" ]]; then
  echo "Processing single issue #$(printf INJECTED)"
  npm start -- --issue $(printf INJECTED) 2>&1 | tee automation.log
fi
```

4. The command substitution executes before `npm` receives its arguments. A local reproduction with the same shell expansion printed `INJECTED`.

No destructive command, secret access, or external callback is needed to demonstrate the behavior.

## Impact
An actor who can dispatch this workflow can execute arbitrary shell commands in the runner context. This job grants `contents: read`, `issues: write`, and `pull-requests: write`. It also runs in the `sep-automation - production` environment and references `APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`. If the environment releases those secrets to the run, injected code could read them and use the GitHub App credentials or webhook according to their configured privileges.

This is a CI workflow command injection and possible privilege escalation from workflow-dispatch permission to the job token and environment secret privileges. It is not an unauthenticated issue and does not require an MCP client or server.

## Remediation
Pass the input through an environment variable, quote it, and validate it before use:

```yaml
env:
  ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.inputs.issue_number }}
run: |
  if [[ -n "$ISSUE_NUMBER" ]]; then
    if ! [[ "$ISSUE_NUMBER" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
      echo "issue_number must be numeric" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    printf "Processing single issue #%s\\n" "$ISSUE_NUMBER"
    npm start -- --issue "$ISSUE_NUMBER" 2>&1 | tee automation.log
  else
    npm start 2>&1 | tee automation.log
  fi
```

Also consider reducing token permissions and reviewing or rotating the referenced secrets if any untrusted run may have occurred.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
